references.title: Formatting text in instructions (Microsoft Writing Style Guide)
references.note: Bold UI labels, code style for typed commands, italic placeholders; describe the action rather than the element type.

references.title: Tutorials (Diátaxis)
references.note: A tutorial teaches by doing: visible results early, expected output, minimal explanation. A framework argued from principle, not a reader study.

references.title: How-to guides (Diátaxis)
references.note: Goal-oriented directions for a competent user; stay on the goal and link out instead of explaining; titles say 'How to ...'.

references.title: Reference (Diátaxis)
references.note: Describe and only describe; consistent, standard patterns that mirror the product; short examples.

references.title: Explanation (Diátaxis)
references.note: Understanding-oriented discussion with context and alternatives; closely bounded; no instruction or description creeping in.

references.title: Notes, cautions, warnings, and other notices (Google developer documentation style guide)
references.note: Note, caution and warning tiers; what must stay in the text flow; too many notices lose their force.

references.authors: US Occupational Safety and Health Administration
references.title: 1910.145: Specifications for accident prevention signs and tags
references.note: Danger and caution tiers for workplace signs and tags. A regulation about signs, not a standard for product manuals.

references.title: API reference code comments (Google developer documentation style guide)
references.note: What an API reference must describe; first sentence, member and method conventions.

references.title: Code samples (Google developer documentation style guide)
references.note: Indentation, 80-column wrapping, preformatted blocks, omissions marked by a comment, an introductory sentence.

references.title: READMEs (Google style guides: docguide)
references.note: A README is a short summary of a directory; the minimum content of a package README.

references.title: Documentation best practices (Google style guides: docguide)
references.note: Small, fresh docs beat a large stale set; change docs with the code; delete dead docs; link rather than duplicate.

references.title: Docs as Code
references.note: Write docs with the tools used for code: version control, review, automated tests. Community claims, no outcome data.

references.title: Effective Troubleshooting
references.note: How to troubleshoot, not how to write a runbook: problem report, triage, hypotheses, tests, notes.

references.title: How API Documentation Fails
references.note: Two surveys of IBM staff: incompleteness, ambiguity and incorrectness hurt most; content matters more than presentation.

references.title: Why You Only Need to Test with 5 Users
references.note: Small repeated tests find most problems; about website interfaces, not instructions.

references.title: Minimalism and Documentation Downsizing (review)
references.note: A secondary account of Carroll's minimalism, not research; minimalism is more than 'less text'.

references.title: Reconstructing minimalism (literature review)
references.note: A student review reporting Carroll, van der Meij and Redish secondhand; its error-time figure is not checked.

references.title: Write accessible documentation (Google developer documentation style guide)
references.note: Keyboard and screen-reader rules, heading levels, link text, alt text, tables, fewer than 26 words per sentence.

references.title: Write for a global audience (Google developer documentation style guide)
references.note: Simple words, short sentences, no phrasal verbs or stacked noun modifiers, consistent terms, for translation.
